groups.text: A Java team wants to call the Kotlin event library.
java C can't read Kotlin.
It reads the class files kotlinc wrote, and some Kotlin features look odd there, or are missing.
First, default arguments.
From Kotlin, PlainBus of refunds works.
From Java, the same call fails: no suitable constructor found.
The class file has only two: the one with every default, and the full one.
@JvmOverloads tells kotlinc to write the ones in between.
Now Java's call compiles.
The reified subscribe is invisible to Java.
It's compiled as a synthetic method, and java C ignores those.
The KClass one works, if Java converts the class by hand.
The fix: an overload that takes a Java Class.
From Java, an object member goes through INSTANCE, and a companion val through Companion and a getter.
@JvmStatic makes publish a real static method.
@JvmField makes SYSTEM a plain static field.
Last, the event.
Its id and amount are value classes, whose init blocks check every value.
In the class file, a value class is just what it wraps.
So Java sees a private constructor that takes a String and a long, and getters with mangled names.
A @JvmName shortcut would let Java pass a raw long straight past init.
The facade does the opposite.
It takes plain values, and builds the value classes itself, so every init block runs.
A good call goes through.
Predict. A Java caller passes seven thousand seven hundred eighty-one, with no pay_ prefix.
What happens?
PaymentId's init throws, just as it would for Kotlin.
Here is the facade in Kotlin, and a Java caller.
The rule. Java sees only the class file.
Give it Class overloads, @JvmOverloads, statics, and a facade that still builds the value classes.
Check yourself. Without @JvmOverloads, does new PlainBus with a name and a flag compile from Java?
Yes. The full constructor is always there.
Only the ones in between are missing.
